text: You just stood up after an hour with your legs crossed and your foot is dead.
Your bottom knee was digging into the side of your top knee.
Right there a nerve wraps around the bone just under the skin.
It powers the muscles that lift your foot and feels the top of it.
And it zips signals down your leg at about one hundred miles an hour.
But your knee pinched it and squeezed shut the tiny blood vessels feeding it.
Starved of oxygen the nerve shuts down and your brain loses your foot.
So the muscle that lifts your foot gets no message and your toes drag.
The second you move blood rushes back in.
And the waking nerve fires wild signals your brain feels as pins and needles.
That tingle is your alarm to move because hours of this can hurt the nerve.
Subscribe because that's why your foot falls asleep.
